mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over the next month reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns in the following 20-day window.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the preceding 30-day average (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS > 4% for 15 consecutive days.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in unemployment benefits (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a weakening labor market and supply-side compression, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >2% while INDPRO decreases by >3% in the same month
regime_hint: labor market softening with supply contraction
failure_condition: 20-day test of negative returns fails to reject the null of no effect (p > 0.05) when trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 2% in the month preceding the decision creates expectations of future rate hikes, which reduces equity valuations and produces negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL exceeds 2% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05) when CPIAUCSL > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) over three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing capacity, which lowers growth expectations and drives negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns show no significant deviation from a baseline of 0% over the prior 12 months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month moving average of the S&P 500 yield (implied by FEDFUNDS) falls below 2.5%, it reflects a flattening of the discount curve that is associated with positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative despite sustained yield curve flattening (measured by 10-year - 2-year spread widening).

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 5% triggers a loss of consumer confidence and delayed corporate hiring, resulting in negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by >0.3 percentage points in a single month
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) when UNRATE crosses above 5%.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both consumer (HOUST) and business (RSAFS) demand series above historical averages for two consecutive months creates a dual tailwind that supports positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both exceed their 12-month averages for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns fail to beat the prior 30-day average (p > 0.05) when both proxies are above average simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: During a supply shock episode (evidenced by a one-time RSAFS drop of >10% in a month), the market anticipates future restocking delays, causing negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by >10% in a single month compared to the prior month
failure_condition: 60-day returns remain non-negative with a p-value > 0.05 when the trigger is detected.
